newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka housing authority hurt by loan defaults.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka housing authority hurt by loan defaults.

text.p: Sri Lanka's National Housing Development Authority (NHDA) is facing financial difficulties due to some 300,000 borrowers defaulting on loan payments, the state-owned Daily News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the NHDA, a self financing state institution, was attempting to recover 1.5 billion rupees from borrowers who had raised loans to build their houses.
It said only 50,000 of some 350,000 borrowers were repaying the loans regularly.
NHDA has given some 3.7 billion rupees in housing loans since 1983, a senior official was quoted as saying.
The official said that NHDA had targeted a monthly recovery of 30 million rupees, but it had been able to get only six million.
But recovery had risen to some 15 million rupees since January this year after NHDA took some of the defaulters to court, the newspaper quoted the official as saying.
The official said NHDA was facing a financial crisis as it needed 20 million rupees a month to just pay salaries to its staff.
He said NHDA was ready to reschedule loan repayments since most of the borrowers had raised small sums, but added the response was not positive.
